answer: Egress Network Flow Tax. Agents route transactions through shifting network paths, paying a routing fee scaled by the shared capacity of correlated clusters. This breaks apart isolated botnets like shale cracking under pressure, forcing malicious nodes to pay exponential fees to maintain synchronized control. A solitary agent operates cheaply within a quiet digital garden, but scaling up an artificial crowd incurs massive routing penalties. Each extra identity adds measurable correlation to the group, which scatters an attacker's capital like fractured light through a cheap opal.
